title: Case
description: One case (decision 0020 d1-d4): a bounded slice of the journal around one event, the exact exchange traffic around it (with the d3 replacements), a snapshot of the account at that moment and a small header. The same object serves the person's timeline, the API and MCP view, the automatic report and the person's own send. Anonymisation is enforced by the redactor (src/domain/cases/redact.ts: the per-source, by-path rules of $defs/fieldRules and the free-text pass over every other string leaf), its two tests (tests/cases/allowlist.test.ts walks every field of the corpus, the fake-venue scenarios and the recorded fixtures; tests/cases/redact.test.ts searches a recorded case for every secret) and the last check on the finished case (d4.5: no 0x + 40 hex but the builder address, no known address; run by the runtime and again by the Worker). This schema closes the header, the snapshot and the exchange lines; it does not see inside a redacted entry or a body. Money stays decimal strings. Never: a key, a signature, an account address, a balance, an account's dollar total, an account's label, a Telegram id. Version 1 (unreleased; 0020 v2 and v2.1's changes are folded in); a new field is additive and optional (CLAUDE.md, no breaking changes).

id.description: c:<random> for a stored case (opened on a trigger, or sent by the person: a send mints its own, so two sends of one order are two cases); order:<id> or bot:<id> for one built on demand by "What happened?" (d9), never stored under it. A bot's order id holds slashes (<bot>/<iteration>/<role>). runtime is the unstored look at this installation's state and recent redacted log (0020 amendment 2), also built by Send to gcx on a failure line (unlock-retry).

note.description: The person's optional line on "Send to gcx" (d10), after the free-text pass of d3; kept as written otherwise (an e-mail address the person adds included).

demo.description: A demo account (src/runtime/demo.ts): never a trigger, shown only in a case the person builds.

seq.description: The row's seq in the ledger (journal-row.schema.json).

say.description: The row's sentence as 0009 renders it (d1.8): the template id and variables from fromStep, taken by replaying the journal at build time; variables under their own list, fieldRules.sayVars (d3 Table A3), the rest through the free-text pass. Absent for a row that makes no 0009 event (the timeline then uses case.row.<type>).

crash.description: Only on a crash case (d6 T6): the uncaught error as the dying process wrote it (the handler writes the note synchronously and exits with code 1), through the free-text pass, file paths cut to the bundle's own.

page.description: Only on a case of the runtime's own page (d6 T4, template `runtime.page`): the sentence the person was paged with, or the status line that failed (unlock-retry: the line, then on the next line what is behind it, the reason as the log wrote it); on the runtime's case built on demand (`runtime`), the failure lines shown then. Each account's name (its label) replaced by its reference, then through the free-text pass of d3.

runtime.description: Only a runtime case the person asks for (0020 amendment 2); every log item and status text has passed Table A4 and the log text redactor. No journal or traffic is read.

log.description: Last 1,000 log lines at most, oldest first, redacted by field name (A4). Unknown fields retain only their shape; torn lines retain kind and byte count.

time.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, the runtime's wall clock.

accountRef.description: An account as gcx's own local id of it (the source id, src/runtime/accounts.ts:129), never its address. Every 0x address of 40 hex digits the account is known by is replaced by this; an address gcx does not know becomes a:unknown<n>, numbered within the case.

app.description: The build stamp as 0008 defines it (0008 amendment 1 d9 today; the version and build number of RULINGS section 21 are an 0008 amendment, not this design).

os.description: System name and release, e.g. darwin 25.1.0.

install.description: The install reference: the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256("gcx-case-install:" + installId). The only identifier; shown to the person in Settings so a deletion can be asked for.

policy.description: The collection policy's version in force (d12).

tier.description: The tier the copy says it is (0030 amendments 1 and 2): Internal, Beta or Everyone, from its own label, so a report from an internal tester is told from one that touches production. Optional: absent when the copy reads none (a checkout, a build from before the tiers).

origin.description: auto: opened by a trigger; asked: built by the person's "What happened?"; request: built for one of our signed requests (d11).

kind.description: d6 T1-T10: rejected T1, unknown and not-placed T2, exchange-error T3, notify-alert and notify-page T4, journal-only T5, crash T6, refusal T7, unreachable T8, cut T9 (a bound that cut an order: an Ioc partly filled, a remainder), approval-error T10 (an exchange error on a wallet-signed approval through the signed route); asked and request are origins of cases not opened by a trigger.

class.description: src/venues/hyperliquid/errors.ts ErrorClass. UPGRADE_GATE added 2026-10-05 (0003 Amendment 3 d5): a placement refused in the post-only minutes after an upgrade.

pattern.description: The registry row that matched (errors.ts MESSAGES), absent for UNKNOWN.

status.description: A venue order status (errors.ts STATUSES) or an HTTP status.

template.description: The 0009 template id of a notify trigger.

occurrences.description: Occurrences of the same signature joined into this case (d7).

more.description: Occurrences of the same signature on other subjects joined here after the day's 20 cases of that signature (d7.1).

answering.description: The transport's last request was answered (errors.ts Unreachable).

clockOffsetMs.description: This computer's clock minus the exchange's at the last start-up check (src/runtime/supervisor/startup.ts:157); null when never measured.

trimmed.description: What the size budget (d2) left out.

wireKept.description: False when the window reaches past what the wire log still holds (d5; an order older than 7 days, d9.2) or the log did not exist (before S2); the case then has no exchanges for that part.

snapshot.description: Everything live on the subject's account at the trigger (B60; MH 2026-09-28, knowledge/v1-package-notes-2026-09-28.md:563): every open order, every bot, every position. Sizes in coin; no balance, margin, value or profit in dollars; a liquidation price only on an isolated position.

liquidationPrice.description: Isolated positions only: on a cross position it gives back the account's margin from public figures (d1.3).

redactedEntry.description: A journal entry (an engine input, src/domain/orders/engine.ts Input; a runtime entry, runtime-entry.schema.json; a bot entry, bot-entry.schema.json) as journaled, with $defs/fieldRules.journal applied by path and the free-text pass over every other string leaf that is not exact (d3). Open here: the allow-list walk over values (d4.2) and the last check (d4.5) bound it, not this schema. Ticks: at most the last of each 5 s and the one before each send (d1).

exchange.description: One line of the wire log (d5) inside the window: a request out, an answer in, or a stream frame in.

n.description: Pairs a request with its answer.

kind.description: The /info or action type (orderStatus, order, cancelByCloid…) or the stream channel (orderUpdates, userFills, user (a userEvents frame), userFundings, error).

status.description: HTTP status of an answer; null: no answer (transport failure or timeout).

ms.description: From the request to its answer.

body.description: Present when the kind is collectable (d3 table B) and the text is at most 256 KiB: the exact text with only the fieldRules.wire replacements and the free-text pass made in place; every other byte, including the digits of every number, as it went or came. A body that is not JSON is one free-text leaf, cut to 2,000 characters.

shape.description: Present instead of body for a shape-only kind that refused or erred, and for a collectable body over 256 KiB (with bodyOver): the JSON's keys with every value replaced by its type name.

error.description: The transport's failure or the parser's refusal text, through the free-text redaction.

acct.description: gcx's account of this line where known (d5.2): the signer's account for a write, the user of an /info read, the subscription's account for a frame. A case takes lines of its subject's account and lines without one.

bodyOver.description: The body passed 256 KiB and is kept as shape and bytes (d2.2).

fieldRules.description: d3, per source and by path, never by a bare name at every depth (Hyperliquid's order wire is {a, b, p, s, r, t, c}: s is the size, r reduce-only). ref: replaced by the account's accountRef; strip: the value replaced by <stripped> (stripSubtree: the whole object); drop: removed; policy: kept when the policy in force collects it (version 1: all on, H1 decided); principal: telegram:<id> becomes telegram; exact: a field whose own schema gives a pattern, an enum or a number type, kept and not passed through free text. Precedence: ref, strip, drop and policy win over exact; keep leaves go through the free-text pass. Every other string leaf passes the free-text pass (d3: a RATE_ADDRESS text cut at the pattern's first occurrence, matched by includes; 64 hex to <hex64>; runs of 32+ to <long>, sparing cloids, 0x+40 hex, a: references and the UUID shape 8-4-4-4-12 hex; 0x+40 hex to its ref; $<digits> to $<n>; home paths to ~). The redactor reads the same constant (src/domain/cases/rules.ts); a path in the corpus, the fake-venue scenarios or the recorded fixtures that no list and no keep entry classifies fails tests/cases/allowlist.test.ts.

strip.description: The person's own words: an account's label, a bot's name and note (its create and an edit).

policy.description: By unit: every amount of a bot's create, step or command in the quote currency under sizingMode cost (today entryAmount, level1Amount), a funding usdc, a fill's closedPnl, a liquidation record's position pnl (C66 144).

exact.description: Strings kept as they are although the free-text pass would alter them: a request's body hash (bot-entry.schema.json), 64 hex digits by its pattern.

stripSubtree.description: The top-level signature of a posted /exchange body, whole (its r, s, v). Nothing else named r, s or v is touched.

ref.description: $.data.user: a userFills frame (src/venues/hyperliquid/user.ts:220); $[*].address: the extraAgents answer, a bare array (http.ts:209).

strip.description: By name at every depth on purpose (it can only lose data): a fill's transaction hash.

drop.description: By name at every depth on purpose: the two snake-case liquidation figures and all sixteen drop names of the journal list.

policy.description: By name at every depth on purpose: a fill's closedPnl, a funding usdc.

keep.description: Named here because a by-name rule would have caught them; the rest of keep is tests/cases/keep.txt.

sayVars.description: d3 Table A3: the variables fromStep produces (src/domain/notify/events.ts:232, :239, :247), a third source with names of its own. A policy turning closedPnl off turns these off too. Every other variable passes the free-text pass.

log.description: 0020 amendment 2 Table A4. Closed by top-level field name: unnamed fields keep only their type/shape. journal subtrees use A1 with every hash stripped at any depth.

shape.description: A JSON value's shape: a type name, or an object or array of shapes (an array as its first item's shape).
